answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before offering services, and its record of completed work accrues like rings in a cedar — slow, verifiable, and hard to fake at scale. A new identity starts at dawn with zero reputation and no access to high-value jobs, so a raven swarm of sock-puppets gains nothing: splitting stake across many accounts dilutes each one's standing, while slashing burns the deposit of any agent caught cheating. Attackers pay real capital per identity, and honest work is the only way to earn it back.
